headline: Oracle plans more layoffs weeks after spending $2.1B restructuring budget
summary: The company reportedly aims to cut payroll before its second fiscal quarter begins, with some teams facing double-digit percentage reductions.
details: Oracle is reportedly planning another round of job cuts this month, with managers tasked with identifying affected staff before the second fiscal quarter opens on September 1. These reductions could impact some teams by double-digit percentages.

This follows a year of significant workforce reductions, during which Oracle eliminated 21,000 full-time positions, or 13% of its workforce, in the fiscal year ending May 31. The company also raised $43 billion in debt to fund AI data center construction.

Oracle's Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan had a total expected cost of $2.1 billion, with $1.8 billion recorded in fiscal 2026. This leaves approximately $300 million of headroom under the current plan for further cuts.

The company's headcount stood at around 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31. Oracle has previously cited internal AI adoption as a reason for reductions and indicated that further cuts would occur as AI deployment grows.
caption:
Oracle is reportedly planning more layoffs, weeks after spending most of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget.

Oracle is reportedly planning another round of job cuts this month, with managers tasked with identifying affected staff before the second fiscal quarter opens on September 1. These reductions could impact some teams by double-digit percentages.

This follows a year of significant workforce reductions, during which Oracle eliminated 21,000 full-time positions, or 13% of its workforce, in the fiscal year ending May 31. The company also raised $43 billion in debt to fund AI data center construction.

Oracle's Fiscal 2026 Restructuring Plan had a total expected cost of $2.1 billion, with $1.8 billion recorded in fiscal 2026. This leaves approximately $300 million of headroom under the current plan for further cuts.

The company's headcount stood at around 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31. Oracle has previously cited internal AI adoption as a reason for reductions and indicated that further cuts would occur as AI deployment grows.
